text:
Maya: Heads-up, we saw ~20% GPU preemptions in us-central over the last hour, causing latency spikes on large-gen jobs.
ops-bot: [alert] preemptible-eviction-spike detected in us-central (GPU pool: preemptible-a), 3 zones affected.
Sam: FWIW this is correlated with a pricing dip on az1-spot — churn pattern looks like short high-frequency evictions.
Liu: Can we ladder fallbacks? Local spot -> regional spot -> reserved warm -> quantized model variant. Keep retries small to avoid amplifying tail latency.
Sam: Agree. Proposed policy (canary):
```
policy:
  - prefer: spot-local
    timeout_ms: 120
  - prefer: spot-regional
    timeout_ms: 250
  - prefer: reserved-warm
    timeout_ms: 400
  - prefer: model-quantized
    fallback: true
```
Maya: For gold tenants, skip spot-regional and go to reserved-warm after 120ms.
Devon: Need to enforce model-compatibility table — not all model shims support quantized variants for function-calls.
Sam: I'll add compatibility gating in router: `if not compatible -> skip_quantized`.
Maya: Cost tradeoffs: if we spill to reserved-warm, estimated cost +8% but 99.9th latency meets SLA. Quantized variant shows -35% cost per-token but output divergence for some evals.
Liu: Add quick evals against our regression suite for top 20 prompts before enabling quantized fallback — sample rate 5%.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: routing-policy update requested by @Sam — canary planned for 30m on us-central with 5% traffic.
Sam: Can someone own rollback threshold? I propose revert if 99th latency > baseline + 40ms or error-rate +0.5%.
Devon: I'll pick rollback and monitoring hooks. Also enable trace-id passthrough to model logs for affected requests.
Maya: Action items: Sam -> patch router & canary; Devon -> monitoring hooks & rollback; Liu -> eval gating; I'll update runbook with cost numbers.
Sam: Patch in PR #4567, will attach tests. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks — let's check back in after the 30m canary. :eyes:
